filters.description: This parameter allows you to filter the supported APIs for the version specified in the URL. You can filter based on three criteria: module, request method, and OAuth scope. The filter syntax is a JSON object with three fields: **field**, **comparator**, and **value**. The **field** can be one of the following: `module`, `operation_types.method`, or `operation_types.oauth_scope`. The **comparator** can be either `equals` or `contains`. Please note that the **Subform** and **multi-module lookup (MxN linking module)** fields are treated as separate modules in Zoho CRM. operations.summary: Process multiple API requests in a single call

rollback_on_fail.description: Specify whether to rollback the composite API request if any of the sub-requests fail. The default value is false. Possible values: **true** - Rollback all operations if any sub-request fails. Workflow automation actions execute only after all sub-requests succeed. **false** - Process each sub-request independently without rollback. This key cannot be **true** when **parallel_execution** is **true**.

parallel_execution.description: Specify whether to process all independent sub-requests (sub-requests with no dependencies/references) in parallel. The default value is true. If "rollback_on_fail" is true, then the default value of this key is false. Possible values: **true** - Execute independent sub-requests in parallel. **false** - Execute sub-requests sequentially. This key cannot be **true** when **rollback_on_fail** is **true**.

__composite_requests.description: Specify the API requests to execute as sub-requests within the composite call.

items.description: Each object represents an individual API sub-request, including the HTTP method, URI, and optional headers, parameters, and body.

method.description: Specify the HTTP method for the corresponding sub-request. Possible values: **GET** - Retrieve data from the API. **POST** - Create a new resource. **PUT** - Update an existing resource. **DELETE** - Remove a resource. **PATCH** - Partially update a resource.

uri.description: Specify the URI path of the corresponding sub-request. The URI must follow the pattern **/crm/{version}/{endpoint}** with the regex `/crm(/.*)?/v[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?/.*`.

sub_request_id.description: Specify a unique identifier for the sub-request. Use this ID to reference the output of this sub-request. The accepted regex is `[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`.

headers.description: Specify the HTTP headers for the sub-request. The **authorization** and **x-crm-org** headers are restricted and cannot be used.

params.description: Specify the parameters for the sub-request.

body.description: Specify the request body for the sub-request. > **Note** > - **Using References in Composite API Requests**: You can reference the output of one sub-request in another within the same API call. > - **Reference Structure**: `@{sub_request_id:JSONPath}` > Where, > - `sub_request_id` is the ID of the sub-request whose response you want to reference. > - `JSONPath` is the path to the specific field in that response. > For example, if you create a Lead in one sub-request (sub_request_id : 1) and need to update it in another, you can use `@{1:$.data[0].details.id}` to dynamically fetch the Lead ID from sub-request 1 and use it in sub-request 2 to modify the same record. > - The `rollback_on_fail` and `parallel_execution` keys cannot both be set to `true`. If both are enabled, the API returns the `AMBIGUITY_DURING_PROCESSING` error. > - All Delete APIs (except Notification APIs) support only record IDs in the URL. Bulk delete operations are not supported. > - When `rollback_on_fail` is `false`: > - Workflows, approvals, and other automation actions are triggered as intended. > - The Composite API consumes one API credit. > - When `rollback_on_fail` is `true`: > - **Workflows** > - Automation actions execute only after all sub-requests complete successfully and no rollback occurs. If one or more sub-requests fail and a rollback happens, the automation actions are not triggered. > - For example, consider the case where a workflow is triggered every time a lead is created with the company name starting with 'S'. In sub-request 1, a lead is created, whose Company name starts with 'S', and sub-request 2 edits the newly created record's company name so that it does not start with 'S'. Only after executing both the sub-requests the workflow will be executed. But in this case, the workflow will not be triggered because the newly created Lead's company name is already updated in sub-request 2, and the criterion for the workflow is not met. Consider another case, where in sub-request 1, a lead is created, whose Company name is 'Silicon Solutions', and sub-request 2 edits this newly created record's website. If none of the other sub-requests change the company name of this newly created record, after executing all the sub-requests successfully, the workflow will be triggered. > - When a rollback occurs, the Composite API consumes one API credit. > - When all sub-requests succeed, the Composite API consumes two API credits. > - Each Composite API request consumes **five concurrency credits**, regardless of the number of sub-requests. > - Each composite API reduces the sub-concurrency by one, while the sub-requests consume their respective sub-concurrencies. ### Allowed APIs The following table gives the list of APIs allowed in a composite request. For these APIs, there are restrictions on the number of records that you can create, update, or delete in a composite request. | API | No. of records allowed | | --- | --- | | Get Org, Get Metadata, Convert a Lead, Get Layout Rules, Get Validation Rules, Get Custom Links, Get/Add/Update Roles, Get Profiles, Get Records' Count, Get/Update Blueprint, Get Variables/Variable Groups, Get Tags, Add/Remove Tags for a record, Get List of Attachments, Delete Photo, Get Currencies, Get Shared Record Details, Get Assignment Rules, Get/Add/Update Pipeline, Get Wizards, Get List of From Addresses, Delete Notifications | No Restriction | | Add/Update/Delete Users, Update/Delink Related Records, Add/Delete Variables, Create/Update/Delete Notes, Create/Update/Merge Tags, Add/Update Currency, Add/Update/PATCH Notifications, Create/Update/Upsert/Delete Records | 1 | | Get Territories, Get Notes, Get Email/Inventory Templates, Get Notifications, Get/Search Records, Get Related Records, Get records through a COQL query, Get Deleted Records, Get Users | 25 |

operations.summary: Get Email Notification Action Usage Reports

group_by.description: Specify the grouping criteria for usage report data. The value must include `date`. Two combinations are accepted: `date` - Returns daily totals; the response omits the resource object, and the count represents the total number of alerts sent that day. `date,resource` - Returns per-action rows with the resource identifier and name populated; type is an optional addition.

type.description: Specify the automation feature type to filter usage data. When omitted, returns usage across all supported feature types. Possible values: workflow_rules - Filters usage data for Workflow Rules. approval_process - Filters usage data for Approval Processes. blueprint - Filters usage data for Blueprint Processes. orchestrations - Filters usage data for Orchestrations. wizards - Filters usage data for Wizards. modules - Filters usage data for module-level limits. email_notifications - Filters usage data for email notification actions. email_templates - Filters usage data for Email Templates. kiosks - Filters usage data for Kiosks. cadences - Filters usage data for Cadences. connected_workflows - Filters usage data for connected workflows.

from.description: Specify the start date (inclusive) for the date range filter, in YYYY-MM-DD format. The date is evaluated in the organization's time zone. When omitted, defaults to 30 days before the value set for the end date parameter. Future dates return an INVALID_DATA error.

to.description: Specify the end date (inclusive) for the query range in YYYY-MM-DD format. Evaluated in the organization's time zone. Defaults to the current date at 23:59:59 when omitted. Future dates return a 400 error with the code INVALID_DATA and the message 'provided_time_is_ahead'.

page.description: Specify the page number to retrieve results from. The first page is page one.

per_page.description: Specify the number of records to return per page. The maximum value is 200.

sort_order.description: Specify the sort order for the results. Possible values: desc - Sorts the results in descending order. asc - Sorts the results in ascending order.

include_inner_details.description: Specify the additional nested fields to include in usage report resource objects. Currently, only `resource.layout_id` is supported, which adds the layout ID inside the resource object when available, primarily for wizard usage rows. Other values are silently ignored.

filters.description: Specify the filter criteria as a JSON-encoded string to narrow the list of email notifications returned. Supported filter field: `field.api_name='name'` with `comparator='contains'`. The value field is dynamic and varies based on the filter input.

items.description: Represents a single per-record entry, containing either the details of the updated record or the error that prevented the record from being updated.

code.description: Represents the result code for the individual record. Possible values: SUCCESS - The record was updated successfully. MANDATORY_NOT_FOUND - A required property is missing from the payload for the record. INVALID_DATA - The request data is invalid for the record. MAPPING_MISMATCH - The provided value violates a field mapping relationship for the record. RECORD_LOCKED - The record is locked and cannot be updated. CONVERTED_RECORD - The record has already been converted and cannot be updated.

details.description: Represents additional details about the response. For an updated record, it contains the record ID along with its creation and modification details. For a failed record, it contains the details of the failure, such as the ID of the record that could not be updated.

message.description: Represents the message describing the result of the operation for this record.

status.description: Represents the status of the operation for this record. Possible values: success - The record was updated. error - The record was not updated.

api_name.description: Specify the unique API name for the module. The name must begin with an English alphabet character, must not end with an underscore, and must not contain two consecutive underscores. If omitted, the system generates the API name from the **plural_label** value.

access_type.description: Specify the access type for the module.Defaults to org_based when omitted. Use team_based to create a team module. Possible values: **org_based** - The module is accessible based on organizational profile settings. **team_based** - The module is restricted to team-based access.

profiles.description: Specify the array of profile IDs that determine which user profiles can access this module. Required for org_based modules. Do not pass this key for team_based modules. Duplicate profile IDs are not allowed.

Supported data types are **autonumber** and **text**. If this is not specified, the system generates a text display field. If data_type is 'autonumber', then auto_number configuration with start_number is mandatory.

field_label.description: Specify the unique display label of the field used as the module's display field. Either this property or **data_type** must be provided when specifying the display field.

data_type.description: Specify the data type of the display field. Possible values: **autonumber** - Automatically generates a unique number sequence for each record. **text** - Allows users to enter text values manually.

auto_number.description: Specify the auto-number configuration for the display field. Required when **data_type** is **autonumber**.

prefix.description: Specify the prefix to prepend to each auto-generated number value in the display field.

start_number.description: Specify the starting number for the auto-number sequence. Only numeric characters are allowed.

suffix.description: Specify the suffix to append to each auto-generated number value in the display field.

criteria.description: Performs search by following the shown criteria: `(({api_name}:{operator}:{value}) and/or ({api_name}:{operator}:{value}))` Performs a search based on the following format: `(({field_API_name}:{operator}:{value}) and/or ({field_API_name}:{operator}:{value}))` Replace `{field_API_name}`, `{operator}`, and `{value}` with the appropriate field API name, condition, and value. **Key Points:** - You can search for a maximum of **10 criteria** (with same or different columns) - The only operator that is supported for **encrypted fields** is `equals` - When using the `equals` operator in the Search API, it behaves like `contains`, retrieving records that include the specified value **Single Condition:** If the condition is `(Company:equals:ABC)`, the response will include records with "ABC" as well as "ABC Inc" in the Company field. **Multiple Conditions:** `equals` still behaves like `contains`. For example, `((Company:equals:ABC) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))`, it retrieves records where the "First Name" starts with "M" and the "Company" contains "ABC" (e.g., "ABC" or "ABC Inc."). **Note:** The above behaviour does not apply to the **picklist field type**. **IN Operator:** The `in` operator checks if a field's value matches any value in a given list. For example, `(Full_Name:in:Patricia,Boyle,Kate)`, it retrieves records where the Full Name is Patricia, Boyle, or Kate. **Special Character Handling:** When a single-line field value contains characters such as `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, `^`, `:`, `-`, `/`, `!`, `?`, `*`, `_`, `@`, space, the Search API returns records with similar-looking values, even if the characters are not an exact match. For example, if Record A has the field value `sales-team@zoho.com` and Record B has `sales_team@zoho.com`, a search using `equals:sales-team@zoho.com` may return both records. **Escaping Special Characters:** When using parentheses `()`, commas `,`, or a backslash `\` as the last character in a search value, follow these steps: 1. Escape special characters using a backslash `\` 2. Encode the value before making the API request. Select the value of the criteria, right-click the value, and choose the EncodeURIComponent option. **Example 1: Escaping Parentheses and Commas** - Search term: `((Last_Name:equals:Burns,B) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))` - Escape the comma `\,`: `((Last_Name:equals:Burns\,B) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))` - Encode the value: `((Last_Name:equals:Burns%5C%2CB) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))` **Example 2: Escaping a Backslash at the End** - Search term: `(Last_Name:equals:K\)` - Escape the backslash `\\`: `(Last_Name:equals:K\\)` - Encode the value: `(Last_Name:equals:K%5C%5C)` **Supported Data Types:** `picklist`, `owner_lookup`, `user_lookup`, `lookup`, `phone`, `email`, `date`, `datetime`, `text`, `textarea`, `integer`, `currency`, `decimal`, `multiselectpicklist`, `bigint`, `percent`, `formula`, `website`, `boolean`, `double` **Supported Operators:** `equals`, `starts_with`, `in`, `not_equal`, `greater_equal`, `greater_than`, `less_equal`, `less_than`, `between` **Operator Compatibility by Data Type:** | Data Type | equals | starts_with | in | not_equal | greater_equal | greater_than | less_equal | less_than | between | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | **text** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **textarea** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **email** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **phone** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **website** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **picklist** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **multiselectpicklist** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **lookup** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **owner_lookup** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **user_lookup** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **boolean** | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **integer** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | **bigint** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | **currency** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | **decimal** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | **double** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | **percent** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | **date** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | **datetime** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | **formula** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | **Legend:** ✓ = Supported, ✗ = Not Supported **Note:** Refer to the Zoho CRM API documentation for the most up-to-date operator compatibility information.

operations.summary: Search Records by Criteria, Word, Email, or Phone

module.description: Specify the API name of the module to search within. Refer to [Get Modules](https://www.zoho.com/crm/developer/docs/api/v8/modules-api.html) to retrieve a list of available modules.

approval_state.description: Specify the approval state to filter records by. The search returns only records in the specified approval state. Possible values: **approval_process_pending**, **webform_invalid**, **review_process_pending**, **webform_invalid_approval**, **zia_vision_validation**, **review_process_rejected**, **webform_unapproved**, **email_parser_waiting**, **approved**, **merge_pending**, **email_parser_rejected**, **zia_vision_rejected**, **zia_vision_pending**, **approval_process_rejected**, **webform_double_optin**.

criteria.description: Specify a criteria string to filter records using field-specific conditions and operators. Performs a search using the following format: `(({field_API_name}:{operator}:{value}) and/or ({field_API_name}:{operator}:{value}))` Replace `{field_API_name}`, `{operator}`, and `{value}` with the appropriate field API name, condition, and value. - You can search using a maximum of 10 criteria, with the same or different fields. - The only operator supported for encrypted fields is `equals`. When using the `equals` operator in the Search API, it behaves like `contains`, retrieving records that include the specified value. For a single condition, if the condition is: `(Company:equals:ABC)` the response includes records with `ABC` as well as `ABC Inc.` in the `Company` field. For multiple conditions, `equals` continues to behave like `contains`. **For example:** `((Company:equals:ABC) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))` This retrieves records where: - `First_Name` starts with `M` - `Company` contains `ABC` (for example, `ABC` or `ABC Inc.`) ** Note**: This behavior does not apply to picklist fields. The `in` operator checks whether a field value matches any value in a given list. **For example:** `(Full_Name:in:Patricia,Boyle,Kate)` This retrieves records where the `Full_Name` is `Patricia`, `Boyle`, or `Kate`. When a single-line field value contains characters such as: `{ } [ ] ^ : - / ! ? * _ @` or spaces, the Search API may return records with similar-looking values, even when the characters are not an exact match. For example: - Record A: `sales-team@zoho.com` - Record B: `sales_team@zoho.com` A search using: `equals:sales-team@zoho.com` may return both records. **Escaping Special Characters** When using parentheses `(` `)`, commas `,`, or a backslash `\` as the last character in a search value: 1. Escape special characters using a backslash (`\`). 2. Encode the value before making the API request. 3. Select the value of the criteria, right-click the value, and choose the `EncodeURIComponent` option. **Example 1: Escaping Parentheses and Commas** Search term: `((Last_Name:equals:Burns,B) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))` Escape the comma: `((Last_Name:equals:Burns\,B) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))` Encode the value: `((Last_Name:equals:Burns%5C%2CB) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))` **Example 2: Escaping a Backslash at the End** Search term: `(Last_Name:equals:K\)` Escape the backslash: `(Last_Name:equals:K\\)` Encode the value: `(Last_Name:equals:K%5C%5C)` **Supported Data Types** - `picklist` - `owner_lookup` - `user_lookup` - `lookup` - `phone` - `email` - `date` - `datetime` - `text` - `textarea` - `integer` - `currency` - `decimal` - `multiselectpicklist` - `bigint` - `percent` - `formula` - `website` - `boolean` - `double` **Supported Operators** - `equals` - `starts_with` - `in` - `not_equal` - `greater_equal` - `greater_than` - `less_equal` - `less_than` - `between` Refer to the following note for operator support by field type. * **Date, DateTime:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `greater_equal`, `greater_than`, `less_equal`, `less_than`, `between`, `in` * **Integer, Currency, Decimal:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `greater_equal`, `greater_than`, `less_equal`, `less_than`, `between`, `in` * **Boolean:** `equals`, `not_equal` * **textarea:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `starts_with` * **Lookup (user/owner):** `equals`, `not_equal`, `in` * **Picklist, Autonumber:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `in` * **Text, Email, Phone, Website:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `starts_with`, `in` * **multiselectpicklist:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `in`, `starts_with` * **bigint:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `greater_than`, `greater_equal`, `less_than`, `less_equal`, `between`, `in` * **percent:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `greater_than`, `greater_equal`, `less_than`, `less_equal`, `between`, `in` * **formula:** Operators depend on the formula return type. Check the corresponding data type's supported operators.

converted.description: Specify whether to filter records by their conversion status. Applicable only for the Leads module. Possible values: **true** - Returns only converted leads. **false** - Returns only unconverted leads. **both** - Returns all leads regardless of conversion status. Defaults to **false**.

word.description: Specify the word or phrase to search for across all searchable text fields in the module. The value must be at least two characters long. Performs a global search with minimum 2 characters required. This is the broadest search method but may be slower than specific field searches. *Mandatory if criteria, email, and phone are not present.*

email.description: Specify the email address to search for across all email-type fields in the module. Partial matches are supported and searches multiple email fields simultaneously. *Mandatory if criteria, phone, and word are not present.*

phone.description: Specify the phone number to search for across all phone-type fields in the module. The value must be at least three characters long and may include digits, spaces, hyphens, parentheses, and the plus sign. Supports various phone number formats including international, national, and partial numbers. *Mandatory if criteria, email, and word are not present.*

fields.description: Specify a comma-separated list of field API names to include in the response. If omitted, the response includes all fields accessible to the current user.

page.description: Specify the page number to retrieve for paginated results. The minimum value is 1. Defaults to 1.

per_page.description: Specify the number of records to return per page. The minimum value is 1, the maximum is 200, and the default is 200.

sort_by.description: Specify the API name of the field to sort the search results by.

sort_order.description: Specify the direction in which to sort the results. Defaults to **desc**. Possible values: **asc** - Ascending order (A-Z, 1-9). **desc** - Descending order (Z-A, 9-1).

type.description: Specify the user type to filter the search results by. Possible values: **ActiveAndDeactive**, **CurrentUser**, **DeletedUsers**, **ParentRoleUsers**, **ChildRoleUsers**, **DeactiveUsers**, **NotConfirmedUsers**, **ConfirmedUsers**, **ActiveUsers**, **AdminUsers**, **ActiveConfirmedAdmins**, **ActiveConfirmedUsers**, **DeveloperUsers**, **SubordinateRoleUsers**, **AllUsers**, **AllActiveUsers**. **Note** - Only one of the mandatory parameters (`criteria`, `email`, `phone`, or `word`) can be used in a single request. - If multiple parameters are provided, the API processes them in the following priority order: 1. `criteria` 2. `email` 3. `phone` 4. `word` - Only the highest-priority parameter in the request is processed. - The `page` and `per_page` parameters help retrieve records based on their position in Zoho CRM. - A single API call can fetch a maximum of 200 records. - To retrieve more records, adjust the `page` and `per_page` values. Example: To fetch 400 records: - First API call: `page=1&per_page=200` -> Fetches records 1-200 - Second API call: `page=2&per_page=200` -> Fetches records 201-400 By making two API calls, all 400 records can be retrieved. - The Search API allows you to search for and retrieve a maximum of 2,000 records. If the search exceeds 2,000 records, the API returns a `LIMIT_REACHED` error. - Values of fields containing sensitive health data are retrieved only when the **Restrict Data Access through API** option in the compliance settings is disabled. If the option is enabled, the field value is returned as `null`. Refer to [HIPAA compliance documentation](https://www.zoho.com/crm/developer/docs/api/v8/hipaa-compliance.html) for more details. - When you create or edit a record and search for it immediately, you may receive a `204 NO CONTENT` response due to indexing delays. To fetch records without delay, use the [Query API](https://www.zoho.com/crm/developer/docs/api/v8/Get-Records-through-COQL-Query.html). - The `in` operator supports up to 100 values. - The `full_name` field contains the concatenated values of the `First Name` and `Last Name` fields. - `full_name` is a read-only field available only in the `Leads`, `Contacts`, and `Users` modules. To retrieve subform records that match your search criteria, use the API name of the corresponding subform module. To retrieve multi-select lookup (MxN) records that match your search criteria, use the API name of the corresponding linking module.

operations.summary: Bulk Search Records by Criteria, Word, Email, or Phone

module.description: Specify the API name of the module to search within. Refer to [Get Modules](https://www.zoho.com/crm/developer/docs/api/v8/modules-api.html) to retrieve a list of available modules.

approval_state.description: Specify the approval state to filter records by. The search returns only records in the specified approval state. Possible values: **approval_process_pending**, **webform_invalid**, **review_process_pending**, **webform_invalid_approval**, **zia_vision_validation**, **review_process_rejected**, **webform_unapproved**, **email_parser_waiting**, **approved**, **merge_pending**, **email_parser_rejected**, **zia_vision_rejected**, **zia_vision_pending**, **approval_process_rejected**, **webform_double_optin**.

criteria.description: Specify a criteria string to filter records using field-specific conditions and operators. Performs a search using the following format: `(({field_API_name}:{operator}:{value}) and/or ({field_API_name}:{operator}:{value}))` Replace `{field_API_name}`, `{operator}`, and `{value}` with the appropriate field API name, condition, and value. - You can search using a maximum of 10 criteria, with the same or different fields. - The only operator supported for encrypted fields is `equals`. When using the `equals` operator in the Search API, it behaves like `contains`, retrieving records that include the specified value. For a single condition, if the condition is: `(Company:equals:ABC)` the response includes records with `ABC` as well as `ABC Inc.` in the `Company` field. For multiple conditions, `equals` continues to behave like `contains`. **For example:** `((Company:equals:ABC) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))` This retrieves records where: - `First_Name` starts with `M` - `Company` contains `ABC` (for example, `ABC` or `ABC Inc.`) ** Note**: This behavior does not apply to picklist fields. The `in` operator checks whether a field value matches any value in a given list. **For example:** `(Full_Name:in:Patricia,Boyle,Kate)` This retrieves records where the `Full_Name` is `Patricia`, `Boyle`, or `Kate`. When a single-line field value contains characters such as: `{ } [ ] ^ : - / ! ? * _ @` or spaces, the Search API may return records with similar-looking values, even when the characters are not an exact match. For example: - Record A: `sales-team@zoho.com` - Record B: `sales_team@zoho.com` A search using: `equals:sales-team@zoho.com` may return both records. **Escaping Special Characters** When using parentheses `(` `)`, commas `,`, or a backslash `\` as the last character in a search value: 1. Escape special characters using a backslash (`\`). 2. Encode the value before making the API request. 3. Select the value of the criteria, right-click the value, and choose the `EncodeURIComponent` option. **Example 1: Escaping Parentheses and Commas** Search term: `((Last_Name:equals:Burns,B) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))` Escape the comma: `((Last_Name:equals:Burns\,B) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))` Encode the value: `((Last_Name:equals:Burns%5C%2CB) and (First_Name:starts_with:M))` **Example 2: Escaping a Backslash at the End** Search term: `(Last_Name:equals:K\)` Escape the backslash: `(Last_Name:equals:K\\)` Encode the value: `(Last_Name:equals:K%5C%5C)` **Supported Data Types** - `picklist` - `owner_lookup` - `user_lookup` - `lookup` - `phone` - `email` - `date` - `datetime` - `text` - `textarea` - `integer` - `currency` - `decimal` - `multiselectpicklist` - `bigint` - `percent` - `formula` - `website` - `boolean` - `double` **Supported Operators** - `equals` - `starts_with` - `in` - `not_equal` - `greater_equal` - `greater_than` - `less_equal` - `less_than` - `between` Refer to the following note for operator support by field type. * **Date, DateTime:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `greater_equal`, `greater_than`, `less_equal`, `less_than`, `between`, `in` * **Integer, Currency, Decimal:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `greater_equal`, `greater_than`, `less_equal`, `less_than`, `between`, `in` * **Boolean:** `equals`, `not_equal` * **textarea:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `starts_with` * **Lookup (user/owner):** `equals`, `not_equal`, `in` * **Picklist, Autonumber:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `in` * **Text, Email, Phone, Website:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `starts_with`, `in` * **multiselectpicklist:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `in`, `starts_with` * **bigint:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `greater_than`, `greater_equal`, `less_than`, `less_equal`, `between`, `in` * **percent:** `equals`, `not_equal`, `greater_than`, `greater_equal`, `less_than`, `less_equal`, `between`, `in` * **formula:** Operators depend on the formula return type. Check the corresponding data type's supported operators.

converted.description: Specify whether to filter records by their conversion status. Applicable only for the Leads module. Possible values: **true** - Returns only converted leads. **false** - Returns only unconverted leads. **both** - Returns all leads regardless of conversion status. Defaults to **false**.

word.description: Specify the word or phrase to search for across all searchable text fields in the module. The value must be at least two characters long. Performs a global search with minimum 2 characters required. This is the broadest search method but may be slower than specific field searches. *Mandatory if criteria, email, and phone are not present.*

email.description: Specify the email address to search for across all email-type fields in the module. Partial matches are supported and searches multiple email fields simultaneously. *Mandatory if criteria, phone, and word are not present.*

phone.description: Specify the phone number to search for across all phone-type fields in the module. The value must be at least three characters long and may include digits, spaces, hyphens, parentheses, and the plus sign. Supports various phone number formats including international, national, and partial numbers. *Mandatory if criteria, email, and word are not present.*

fields.description: Specify a comma-separated list of field API names to include in the response. If omitted, the response includes all fields accessible to the current user.

page.description: Specify the page number to retrieve for paginated results. The minimum value is 1. Defaults to 1.

per_page.description: Specify the number of records to return per page. The minimum value is 1, the maximum is 200, and the default is 200.

sort_by.description: Specify the API name of the field to sort the search results by.

sort_order.description: Specify the direction in which to sort the results. Defaults to **desc**. Possible values: **asc** - Ascending order (A-Z, 1-9). **desc** - Descending order (Z-A, 9-1).

type.description: Specify the user type to filter the search results by. Possible values: **ActiveAndDeactive**, **CurrentUser**, **DeletedUsers**, **ParentRoleUsers**, **ChildRoleUsers**, **DeactiveUsers**, **NotConfirmedUsers**, **ConfirmedUsers**, **ActiveUsers**, **AdminUsers**, **ActiveConfirmedAdmins**, **ActiveConfirmedUsers**, **DeveloperUsers**, **SubordinateRoleUsers**, **AllUsers**, **AllActiveUsers**. **Note** - Only one of the mandatory parameters (`criteria`, `email`, `phone`, or `word`) can be used in a single request. - If multiple parameters are provided, the API processes them in the following priority order: 1. `criteria` 2. `email` 3. `phone` 4. `word` - Only the highest-priority parameter in the request is processed. - The `page` and `per_page` parameters help retrieve records based on their position in Zoho CRM. - A single API call can fetch a maximum of 200 records. - To retrieve more records, adjust the `page` and `per_page` values. Example: To fetch 400 records: - First API call: `page=1&per_page=200` -> Fetches records 1-200 - Second API call: `page=2&per_page=200` -> Fetches records 201-400 By making two API calls, all 400 records can be retrieved. - The Search API allows you to search for and retrieve a maximum of 2,000 records. If the search exceeds 2,000 records, the API returns a `LIMIT_REACHED` error. - Values of fields containing sensitive health data are retrieved only when the **Restrict Data Access through API** option in the compliance settings is disabled. If the option is enabled, the field value is returned as `null`. Refer to [HIPAA compliance documentation](https://www.zoho.com/crm/developer/docs/api/v8/hipaa-compliance.html) for more details. - When you create or edit a record and search for it immediately, you may receive a `204 NO CONTENT` response due to indexing delays. To fetch records without delay, use the [Query API](https://www.zoho.com/crm/developer/docs/api/v8/Get-Records-through-COQL-Query.html). - The `in` operator supports up to 100 values. - The `full_name` field contains the concatenated values of the `First Name` and `Last Name` fields. - `full_name` is a read-only field available only in the `Leads`, `Contacts`, and `Users` modules. To retrieve subform records that match your search criteria, use the API name of the corresponding subform module. To retrieve multi-select lookup (MxN) records that match your search criteria, use the API name of the corresponding linking module.

filters.description: **`filters` Parameter** The `filters` parameter is used to filter responses from the Timeline API based on specific conditions. Each filter condition consists of the following components: - field` - `comparator` - `value` **Supported `field.api_name` Values** The following values are supported for `field.api_name`: - `record.module.api_name` - `source` - `audited_time` - `done_by.id` **`record.module.api_name`** Use this field to filter timeline details related to the following record types: - `Notes` - `Attachments` - `Tasks` - `Calls` - `Events` - `Emails` **Allowed Comparators** - `equal` - `in` **Allowed Values** - `Notes` - `Attachments` - `Tasks` - `Calls` - `Events` - `Emails` **Example: Filter Notes** ```json { "field": { "api_name": "record.module.api_name" }, "comparator": "equal", "value": "Notes" } ``` **Example: Filter Notes and Tasks** ```json { "field": { "api_name": "record.module.api_name" }, "comparator": "in", "value": ["Notes", "Tasks"] } ``` **`done_by.id`** Use this field to filter timeline details performed by a specific user. **Allowed Comparators** - `equal` - `in` **Allowed Values** - User IDs **Example** ```json { "field": { "api_name": "done_by.id" }, "comparator": "in", "value": ["5843104000000424001"] } ``` **`audited_time`** Use this field to filter timeline data based on the audit timestamp. **Allowed Comparator** - `between` **Allowed Values** - Time in ISO 8601 format **Example: Filter Timeline Details Between Two Dates** ```json { "field": { "api_name": "audited_time" }, "comparator": "between", "value": [ "2023-10-25T00:00:00+12:00", "2023-10-30T23:59:59+12:00" ] } ``` **`source`** Use this field to filter timeline data based on its source. **Allowed Comparators** - `equal` - `in` **Allowed Values** - `crm_api` - `mass_delete_via_crm_api` - `bulkapi` - `approval_process` - `assignment_rules` - `blueprint` - `mass_update_via_blueprint` - `orchestration` - `convert` - `massconvert` - `custom_function` - `macro` - `crm_ui` - `mass_update` - `mass_update_via_scheduler` - `mass_delete_via_clean_up` - `bulk_action` - `change_owner` - `mass_change_owner_via_scheduler` - `review_process` - `scoringrule` - `wizard` - `workflow` **Example: Filter by a Single Source** ```json { "field": { "api_name": "source" }, "comparator": "equal", "value": "crm_ui" } ``` **Example: Filter by Multiple Sources** ```json { "field": { "api_name": "source" }, "comparator": "in", "value": ["crm_api", "crm_ui"] } ``` --- **Combining Multiple Conditions** Use `group_operator` and `group` to combine multiple filter conditions. **Example** ```json { "group_operator": "AND", "group": [ { "field": { "api_name": "record.module.api_name" }, "comparator": "in", "value": ["Notes"] }, { "field": { "api_name": "source" }, "comparator": "in", "value": ["crm_ui", "crm_api"] } ] } ``` You can also refer to the sample request for the complete structure. > **Note:** The value of the `filters` parameter must be URL-encoded before sending the request. **URL Encoding Example** The following filter: ```json { "comparator": "between", "field": { "api_name": "audited_time" }, "value": [ "2023-06-07T00:00:00+05:30", "2023-06-07T12:59:59+05:30" ] } ``` is encoded as: ```text filters=%7B%22comparator%22%3A%22between%22%2C%22field%22%3A%7B%22api_name%22%3A%22audited_time%22%7D%2C%22value%22%3A%5B%222023-06-07T00%3A00%3A00%2B05%3A30%22%2C%222023-06-07T12%3A59%3A59%2B05%3A30%22%5D%7D ``` You can use the **Encode URL** and **Decode URL** options in the [URL Encoder/Decoder tool](https://www.zoho.com/toolkit/encode-decode.html) to encode or decode this value.

module.description: Specify the API name of the CRM module for which enrichment is to be triggered. Use the [Get Modules API](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) to retrieve the list of valid module API names.

record_id.description: Specify the unique identifier of the record for which enrichment is to be triggered. When omitted, the job runs at the module level. Use the records API of the target module to retrieve record identifiers.

__zia_org_enrichment.description: Specify the list of enrichment requests to schedule. You can supply up to 50 entries in a single call.

items.description: Represents a single Zia organization enrichment request that defines the trigger fields used to identify the organization.

enrich_based_on.description: Specify the details of the fields on whose values you want to trigger enrichment. Note that you must provide at least one of the following values in the input. Based on these values, Zia will look for information on the web and enrich fields as per [Enrichment Configuration.](zia_enrichment.yaml#$.paths./settings/zia/data_enrichment.get)) Note that the values of these keys must be at least three characters long and only in English.

name.description: Specify the name of the organization that Zia uses as a trigger value to look up enrichment data.

email.description: Specify the email address of the organization that Zia uses as a trigger value to look up enrichment data.

website.description: Specify the website domain of the organization that Zia uses as a trigger value to look up enrichment data.

code.description: Indicates the scheduling outcome of the enrichment request. Possible values: **SCHEDULED** - The enrichment job has been queued for asynchronous execution. Example: "SCHEDULED".

id.description: Shows the unique identifier assigned to the scheduled enrichment job. Use this identifier with GET `/__zia_org_enrichment/{id}` to retrieve job status and enriched data.

details.description: Contains identifying information about the scheduled enrichment job.

message.description: Provides a message that describes the outcome of the scheduling request.

status.description: Indicates whether the scheduling request succeeded. Possible values: **success** - The enrichment job was successfully accepted and queued. Example: "success".

items.description: Represents the scheduling result of a single enrichment request.

__zia_org_enrichment.description: Contains the list of scheduling results, one entry per submitted enrichment request.

output.description: Defines the response body returned when a Zia organization enrichment job is successfully scheduled.

id.description: Specify the unique identifier of the Zia organization enrichment job to retrieve. Obtain this value from the response of POST `/__zia_org_enrichment` or from the listing returned by GET `/__zia_org_enrichment`.

output.description: Defines the response body returned when the requested organization enrichment job is retrieved successfully.

__zia_org_enrichment.description: Contains the details of the requested organization enrichment job.

items.description: Represents the full record of a single organization enrichment job, including its trigger fields and enriched output.

id.description: Shows the unique identifier of the organization enrichment job.

status.description: Indicates the current execution status of the enrichment job. Possible values: **COMPLETED** - The job has finished and enriched data is available. **SCHEDULED** - The job is queued and yet to run. **FAILED** - The job ended in a failure. **DATA_NOT_FOUND** - The job completed but Zia could not locate public data to enrich.

enrich_based_on.description: Shows the trigger values that were supplied when the enrichment job was scheduled.

name.description: Shows the organization name that was used as a trigger value.

email.description: Shows the email address that was used as a trigger value.

website.description: Shows the website domain that was used as a trigger value.

enriched_data.description: Contains the data retrieved by Zia for the organization. The keys present in this object depend on the fields configured in the enrichment configuration of the organization. Returns `null` when the job has not yet completed or when no public data could be retrieved.

page.description: Specify the page number to retrieve the list of records from the paginated results. Default value is 1. Accepts only positive integer values.

per_page.description: Specify the number of records to retrieve per page. Default and maximum value is 100.

sort_by.description: Specify the field to use for sorting the response based on created time. Accepts the literal value `created_time`.

sort_order.description: Specify the direction(ascending or descending) in which to sort the response. Possible values: **asc** - Sort results in ascending order. **desc** - Sort results in descending order.

status.description: Filter the response by the status of the scheduled enrichment job, using the create org enrichment API. Possible values: **COMPLETED** - Returns jobs that finished and produced enriched data. **FAILED** - Returns jobs that ended with a failure. **DATA_NOT_FOUND** - Returns jobs that completed but could not locate any public data to enrich. **SCHEDULED** - Returns jobs that are queued and yet to run.

output.description: Defines the response body returned when the list of organization enrichment jobs is retrieved successfully.

align.description: Represents the alignment of the webform on the page. Possible values: **right** - Align the form to the right. **left** - Align the form to the left. **top** - Align the form to the top.

help.description: Represents the help configuration for the field, including help text and an optional URL. Returns null when no help is configured.

hidden.description: Indicates whether the field is hidden on the webform. Possible values: **true** - The field is hidden from visitors. **false** - The field is visible to visitors.

date_format.description: Represents the date format used for date fields in the webform. Returns null when no date format is specified.

required.description: Indicates whether the field is required on the webform. Possible values: **true** - The field must be filled in before the form can be submitted. **false** - The field is optional.

default_value.description: Represents the default value pre-populated in the hidden field on the webform.

suggestion.description: Represents the AI-generated suggestion for the AB test, if available. Returns null when no suggestion is available.

name.description: Represents the name of the AB test configuration.

status.description: Represents the current lifecycle status of the AB test. Possible values: **drafted** - The test exists but has not started. **running** - The test actively distributes traffic. **scheduled** - The test starts at a future date. **paused** - The test has stopped temporarily. **completed** - The test has finished and results are available. **launched** - The winning form has launched.

AbTestingModuleNested.description: Represents the CRM module associated with an AB test, identified by its API name and ID.

dynamic_allocation_by_zia.description: Indicates whether the traffic allocation between the base form and variant forms is managed dynamically by Zia, the AI assistant. Possible values: **true** - Zia dynamically adjusts traffic allocation based on performance. **false** - Traffic is allocated according to the manually configured split.

code.description: Represents the response code returned for the AB test operation.

notify.description: Indicates whether notifications are enabled for this AB test. Possible values: **true** - Notifications are sent when the test reaches a significant milestone. **false** - No notifications are sent.

traffic_diversion.description: Represents the traffic diversion configuration for the AB test, if applicable. Returns null when no traffic diversion is configured.

variant_form.description: Represents the list of variant webforms included in the AB test, each with its own traffic allocation and performance data.

pause_resume_info.description: Represents information about a pause or resume action on the AB test, if applicable. Returns null when no pause or resume action has occurred.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the AB test configuration.

traffic.description: Represents the total percentage of visitor traffic allocated to this AB test.

created_time.description: Represents the creation date and time of the AB test configuration.

complete_restart_info.description: Represents information about a complete restart of the AB test, if applicable. Returns null when no restart has occurred.

started_time.description: Represents the actual date and time when the AB test started running.

suggestion.description: Represents the AI-generated suggestion for the AB test, if available. Returns null when no suggestion is available.

start_time.description: Represents the scheduled start time of the AB test.

visitors.description: Represents the total number of visitors who have been exposed to the AB test.

name.description: Represents the name of the AB test configuration.

days.description: Represents the number of days the AB test has been running.

status.description: Represents the current lifecycle status of the AB test. message.description: Represents the message describing the result of the AB test operation.

AcknowledgeVisitorNested.description: Represents the auto-response configuration for acknowledging a visitor after webform submission, including the Email Template and reply-to address.

template_name.description: Represents the name of the Email Template used to acknowledge the visitor upon webform submission.

template_id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the Email Template used to send an acknowledgment message to the visitor upon webform submission.

ActionAttachment.description: Represents a single attachment entry for a note created by the add note action. Each entry contains a merge field reference to a File Upload field.

id.description: Represents a merge field reference to a File Upload field. Three formats are supported: (1) Record field — `${!<kiosk_group_api_name>.<resource_api_name>.<field_api_name>}`, where the resource is `CurrentRecord` or a GetRecord API name (for example, `GetRecords_1`). (2) CRM module field — `${!<module_api_name>.<field_api_name>}`, for example, `${!users.email}`. (3) Kiosk screen field — `${!<kiosk_group_api_name>.<screen_field_api_name>}`, which references a File Upload field on a kiosk screen.

ActionCreateDetails.description: Represents the details configuration object for a kiosk action state. The structure is composed using allOf to include one or more optional action-type properties depending on the configured action.

execute_for_record.description: For associate actions and few non associate actions, the action should be performed on a specific record in the CRM system. For example, if the user is creating the field update action to modify a company name, he must provide which record's company name should be changed. So, he should provide either a get record reference or a current record reference in "execute_for_record" key. ID and name of the resource will be enough. However, for actions which are unrelated for a specific record, this key can be ignored.

add_tags.description: Configuration for the add_tags action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json.

note.description: Configuration used to create a note associated with a CRM record. For example, a specific Lead detail view page can have a note by running this particular action.

functions.description: Associates an action that triggers a function for records fetched via get record or current record.

open_record.description: It is an action to open a particular record fetched from the CRM modules. The user will configure either a get record or a current record with this action. The fetched record is opened automatically when the action is executed.

get_record.description: This is the JSON which contains the association details of the get_record component for a get_records state.

criteria.description: Criteria for ownership assignment comparison. Referenced from Criterion.json.

open_link.description: Open link is an action used to open a specific link which is configured during state creation when triggered. This json will consist of the link and encoding details.

convert.description: Configuration for the convert action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json.

type.description: Indicates the action type for the kiosk action state. The specified type determines which action configuration object must be present in the details object.

create_record.description: Configuration for the create_record action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json.

assign_owner.description: Configuration for the assign_owner action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json.

remove_tags.description: Configuration for the remove_tags action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json.

add_meeting.description: Configuration for the add_meeting action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json.

webhooks.description: Associates an action that triggers a webhook for records fetched via get record or current record.

Three formats are supported: (1) Record field — `${!<kiosk_group_api_name>.<resource_api_name>.<field_api_name>}`, where the resource is `CurrentRecord` or a GetRecord API name. (2) CRM module field — `${!<module_api_name>.<field_api_name>}`, for example, `${!users.email}`. (3) Kiosk screen field — `${!<kiosk_group_api_name>.<screen_field_api_name>}`.

email_notifications.description: Associates an action that triggers an email notification for records fetched via get record or current record.

field_updates.description: Associates an action that updates a field's value in a record fetched via get record or current record.

quick_create_record.description: It is an action used to quickly configure a create record action with minimal field input. However, there will be a pop up during the execution of the action where the user must provide the values for the fields configured. Then, the record will be created.

tasks.description: Associates an action that triggers a task for records fetched via get record or current record.

schedule_call.description: Configuration for the schedule_call action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json.

ActionUpdateDetails.description: Represents the details configuration object for updating a kiosk action state. The structure is composed using allOf to include one or more optional action-type properties depending on the configured action.

execute_for_record.description: For associate actions and few non associate actions, the action should be performed on a specific record in the CRM system. For example, if the user is creating the field update action to modify a company name, he must provide which record's company name should be changed. So, he should provide either a get record reference or a current record reference in "execute_for_record" key. ID and name of the resource will be enough. However, for actions which are unrelated for a specific record, this key can be ignored.

add_tags.description: Configuration for the add_tags action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json. MANDATORY: id (state id), and id (action's id inside "details") is mandatory for update.

note.description: Configuration used to create a note associated with a CRM record. For example, a specific Lead detail view page can have a note by running this particular action.

functions.description: Functions is an associated action which will execute a piece of code or other operations upon execution. These functions would have been created either previously or during the creation of the action which can be associated and run during action execution. It acts as a server-side function executed when kiosk is executed.

open_record.description: It is an action to open a particular record fetched from the CRM modules. The user will configure either a get record or a current record with this action. The fetched record is opened automatically when the action is executed.

get_record.description: This is the JSON which contains the association details of the get_record component for a get_records state.

criteria.description: Criteria for ownership assignment comparison. Referenced from Criterion.json.

open_link.description: Open link is an action used to open a specific link which is configured during state creation when triggered. This json will consist of the link and encoding details.

convert.description: Configuration for the convert action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json. MANDATORY: id (state id), and id (action's id inside "details") is mandatory for update.

type.description: Indicates the action type for the kiosk action state. The specified type determines which action configuration object must be present in the details object.

create_record.description: Configuration for the create_record action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json. MANDATORY: id (state id), and id (action's id inside "details") is mandatory for update.

assign_owner.description: Configuration for the assign_owner action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json. MANDATORY: id (state id), and id (action's id inside "details") is mandatory for update.

remove_tags.description: Configuration for the remove_tags action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json. MANDATORY: id (state id), and id (action's id inside "details") is mandatory for update.

add_meeting.description: Configuration for the add_meeting action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json. MANDATORY: id (state id), and id (action's id inside "details") is mandatory for update.

webhooks.description: Represents a webhook action that triggers an external HTTP callback when executed. The webhook configuration can be done during the creation of the state. However, these configuration details won't come in the webhook action payload. The payload will only refer the webhook created.

api_name.description: Represents the merge field API name used to dynamically resolve the owner for the assign_owner action. When the user is not provided directly, the merge field expression identifies the user. Supported formats: (1) Record field: `${!<kiosk_group_api_name>.<resource_api_name>.<field_api_name>}` where resource can be `CurrentRecord` or a GetRecord API name. (2) CRM module field: `${!<module_api_name>.<field_api_name>}` for example, `${!users.email}`. (3) Kiosk screen field: `${!<kiosk_group_api_name>.<screen_field_api_name>}`.

email_notifications.description: Email notifications action will be used to trigger emails with pre-defined template and content to the configured records. This is an associate action and hence this JSON will consist of the email notification action's identifiers like ID and name. It is mandatory for the action to be created before associating in the Kiosk. A specific action can be associated with only one state in the Kiosk.

field_updates.description: In case the action type is "field_updates", this key is mandatory. It contains the information or identifier of the "Field update" action configured in the workflow. If we give ID of the configured action, it will be associated here. It is mandatory for this field update action id to be associated in only one place or state of the Kiosk. You cannot a single field update action in many action states.

quick_create_record.description: It is an action used to quickly configure a create record action with minimal field input. However, there will be a pop up during the execution of the action where the user must provide the values for the fields configured. Then, the record will be created.

tasks.description: Tasks is another associate action which helps in assigning tasks to specific records. This JSON will consist of the resource identifiers for the Tasks action in the workflow.

schedule_call.description: Configuration for the schedule_call action. Referenced from AutomationNonAssociateActions.json. MANDATORY: id (state id) is mandatory for update.

ActionsAllowed.description: Represents the set of Boolean permission flags indicating which modification operations are permitted on a layout section, such as adding fields, renaming, reordering, and deleting.

add_field.description: Indicates whether new fields may be introduced into the layout section. Possible values: `true` — adding fields to the section is permitted; `false` — adding fields to the section is not permitted.

rename.description: Indicates whether the display name of the layout section may be changed. Possible values: `true` — renaming the section is permitted; `false` — renaming the section is not permitted.

change_tab_traversal.description: Indicates whether the keyboard tab traversal order of fields within the layout section may be modified. Possible values: `true` — changing the tab traversal order is permitted; `false` — changing the tab traversal order is not permitted.

reorder.description: Indicates whether the relative ordering of sections or fields within the layout may be changed. Possible values: `true` — reordering is permitted; `false` — reordering is not permitted.

delete.description: Indicates whether the layout section may be permanently removed from the layout. Possible values: `true` — deleting the section is permitted; `false` — deleting the section is not permitted.

remove_field.description: Indicates whether existing fields may be detached from the layout section. Possible values: `true` — removing fields from the section is permitted; `false` — removing fields from the section is not permitted.

change_column_count.description: Indicates whether the number of columns displayed within the layout section may be modified. Possible values: `true` — adjusting the column count for the section is permitted; `false` — adjusting the column count for the section is not permitted.
