active.description: Indicates whether the portal form is active. Possible values: true - The portal form is active. false - The portal form is inactive.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the portal configured for the webform.

WebhookActionInputEntry.description: Represents a request payload entry for an after action of type **webhooks**. Only the id and name properties are accepted for this entry.

name.description: Represents the name of the after action associated with the transition.

id.description: Represents the ID of the after action associated with the transition.

type.description: Indicates the type of the after action of the transition. Possible values: **webhooks**. Example: "webhooks".

WebhookAuthenticationDetails.description: Represents the authentication configuration for the webhook endpoint. Use type **general** for endpoints that do not require credentials. Use type **connection** with a valid connection_name for endpoints that require authenticated access via a pre-configured Zoho connection.

connection_name.description: Represents the name of the Zoho connection used for authentication. This field is required only when **type** is **connection**.

type.description: Specify the authentication method for the webhook endpoint. Possible values: **general** - No credentials required. **connection** - Uses a pre-configured Zoho connection.

WebhookCreateInput.description: Represents the writable fields for creating a new webhook. Required fields are name, module, url, http_method, authentication, and feature_type. System-managed fields must not be included. Refer to the [Get Modules](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) resource for valid module API names.

name.description: Specify the display name of the webhook. The name must not contain the tilde (~) character.

module.description: The CRM module this webhook is associated with. Provide at least one of api_name or id. Cannot be changed after creation.

url.description: Specify the destination URL that receives the webhook request when triggered. The URL must begin with http://, https://, www., or a merge-field token (${...}). URLs resolving to internal or private host addresses are rejected by SSRF protection.

http_method.description: Specify the HTTP method used when the webhook fires. POST and PUT accept headers and body. GET and DELETE accept url_parameters. DELETE also accepts headers. Possible values: **POST** - Sends a POST request. **GET** - Sends a GET request. **PUT** - Sends a PUT request. **DELETE** - Sends a DELETE request.

authentication.description: Authentication configuration. Required for all webhooks, including those without authentication credentials. Use type=general for webhooks that do not require authentication (no connection_name needed). Use type=connection when the webhook endpoint requires authenticated access via a pre-configured connection (connection_name is required).

description.description: Specify the optional description of the webhook purpose.

related_module.description: Related CRM module. Required when feature_type is kiosk. Null otherwise.

feature_type.description: Specify the automation feature type for this webhook. Possible values: **workflow** - Workflow Rule. **approval_process** - Approval Process. **blueprint_transition** - Blueprint transition. **blueprint_state** - Blueprint state. **assignment_rules** - Assignment Rules. **kiosk** - Kiosk feature. **commandcenter_service** - CommandCenter service.

headers.description: HTTP headers for the outgoing webhook request. Only allowed when http_method is POST, PUT, or DELETE. Restricted header name: HOST is not allowed. Parameter names must be unique across the collection (DUPLICATE_DATA).

url_parameters.description: URL query parameters for the outgoing request. Only allowed when http_method is GET or DELETE.

body.description: Request body configuration. Only allowed when http_method is POST or PUT. type and format are required. When type=form_data: provide form_data_content (object with module_parameters and custom_parameters arrays); When type=raw: provide raw_data_content (string) and format (JSON, XML, Text, or HTML). When type=none: format may be null.

date_time_format.description: Optional. Only relevant when a date or datetime merge-field is used in any parameter (headers, url_parameters, or body). Use datetime_format + time_zone when a datetime field is referenced (e.g., ${!Leads.Created_Time}). Use date_format when a date field is referenced (e.g., ${!Leads.Date_1}). Ignored if no date/datetime merge-fields are present.

WebhookCustomParameters.description: Represents a static key-value parameter for webhook requests. Used in headers, URL query parameters, or form data fields. The value is a fixed literal sent unchanged with every webhook execution.

name.description: Represents the parameter key sent in the webhook request.

value.description: Represents the static literal value sent with every webhook execution.

WebhookDetailsResponse.description: Represents the nested object containing the unique identifier of the webhook returned by a mutation operation.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the webhook.

WebhookFailureDetail.description: Represents the details of a single webhook execution failure, including the triggering CRM record, workflow rule, failure reason, and timestamp.

webhook.description: Reference to the webhook that failed (id and name).

entity_details.description: Details of the CRM record that triggered the failed webhook execution.

failure_time.description: Represents the ISO 8601 timestamp of when the webhook execution failed.

failure_reason.description: Represents the reason for the webhook execution failure, such as page_notfound.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the failure record.

workflow_rule.description: Reference to the workflow rule that triggered the webhook.

WebhookFailuresResponse.description: Represents the paginated response containing webhook execution failure records. Filter by webhook_id, module API name, and date range using query parameters.

webhook_failures.description: Represents the list of webhook execution failure detail objects.

info.description: Pagination metadata for navigating failure records.

WebhookHeaders.description: Represents the HTTP headers configuration for the outgoing webhook request. Supports module merge-field parameters and custom static parameters. The host header name is reserved and cannot be used.

custom_parameters.description: Represents the static key-value pairs sent as HTTP headers with every webhook execution.

module_parameters.description: Represents the module merge-field parameters sent as HTTP headers. The key must be present but may be an empty array when only custom parameters are needed.

WebhookModuleParameters.description: Represents a module merge-field parameter for webhook requests. Used in headers, URL query parameters, or form data fields. The value is resolved at runtime from the field of the triggering CRM record.

name.description: Represents the parameter key sent in the webhook request. The name must be unique within the parameter collection.

value.description: Represents the merge-field token resolved at runtime from the triggering CRM record. Use the API field names and not display names (for example, use ${!Leads.Last_Name}, not ${!Leads.Last Name}). Invalid API names return INVALID_DATA.

WebhookReference.description: Represents a lightweight reference to a webhook, containing its unique identifier and display name. Used in failure log records.

name.description: Represents the display name of the webhook.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the webhook.

WebhookRequestBody.description: Represents the request body configuration for the outgoing webhook request. For type **form_data**, provide form_data_content with module_parameters and custom_parameters; format may be null. For type **raw**, supply raw_data_content and a format value of JSON, XML, Text, or HTML. For type **none**, the body carries no content and format may be null.

format.description: Specify the body content format. Possible values: **JSON** - JSON format. **XML** - XML format. **Text** - Plain text format. **HTML** - HTML format. **null** - Valid for form_data and none body types.

raw_data_content.description: Represents the raw string content sent as the request body. This field is required when the body type is raw.

type.description: Specify the body type for the webhook request. Possible values: **form_data** - Sends data as key-value pairs in the request body. **raw** - Sends plain text, JSON, HTML, or XML content directly. **none** - No body content.

form_data_content.description: Form data content when body type is form_data. Contains module parameters, custom parameters, and an optional user-defined parameter.

WebhookStatusResponse.description: Represents the operation result for a webhook create, update, or delete action. On success, code is success, status is success, and details contains the webhook ID.

code.description: Represents the success or error code of the webhook operation.

details.description: Result details. On success, contains the webhook id.

message.description: Represents the description of the operation result.

status.description: Represents the operation status.

WebhookUpdateInput.description: Represents the writable fields for updating an existing webhook. Full-replacement semantics apply all required fields must be present, as omitted fields reset to defaults or null. The module field is immutable; providing a different module returns NOT_ALLOWED. System-managed read-only fields must be omitted.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the webhook to update. The ID is required in the request body when using the bulk update endpoint.

name.description: Specify the display name of the webhook. The name must not contain the tilde (~) character. The name cannot be changed for kiosk feature actions.

module.description: The CRM module. Cannot be changed - providing a different module returns NOT_ALLOWED.

url.description: Specify the destination URL that receives the webhook request when triggered. The URL must begin with http://, https://, www., or a merge-field token (${...}). URLs resolving to internal or private host addresses are rejected by SSRF protection.

http_method.description: Specify the HTTP method used when the webhook fires. Possible values: **POST** - Sends a POST request. **GET** - Sends a GET request. **PUT** - Sends a PUT request. **DELETE** - Sends a DELETE request.

description.description: Specify the optional description of the webhook purpose.

related_module.description: Related CRM module. Required when feature_type is kiosk.

feature_type.description: Specify the automation feature type for this webhook. Possible values: **workflow** - Workflow Rule. **approval_process** - Approval Process. **blueprint_transition** - Blueprint transition. **blueprint_state** - Blueprint state. **assignment_rules** - Assignment Rules. **kiosk** - Kiosk feature. **commandcenter_service** - CommandCenter service.

headers.description: HTTP headers. Only allowed when http_method is POST, PUT, or DELETE. Restricted header name: HOST is not allowed. Parameter names must be unique (DUPLICATE_DATA).

url_parameters.description: URL query parameters. Only allowed when http_method is GET or DELETE.

body.description: Request body. Only allowed when http_method is POST or PUT. type and format are required. When type=form_data: provide form_data_content (object with module_parameters and custom_parameters arrays); format may be null. When type=raw: provide raw_data_content (string) and format (JSON, XML, Text, or HTML). When type=none: format may be null.

date_time_format.description: Optional. Only relevant when a date or datetime merge-field is used in any parameter (headers, url_parameters, or body). Use datetime_format + time_zone for datetime fields, date_format for date fields. Ignored if no date/datetime merge-fields are present.

WebhookUrlParameters.description: Represents the URL query parameters appended to the webhook request URL. Applicable only when http_method is GET or DELETE. Returns null when http_method is POST or PUT.

custom_parameters.description: Represents the static key-value pairs appended as URL query parameters to every webhook request. Each entry must have a unique name. - name (string, optional) Specify a name to the custom header. - value (string, optional) Specify a value to the custom header. "custom_parameters": [ { "name": "OAuth", "value": "2.0" } ]. A maximum of 10 entries is allowed.

module_parameters.description: Represents the module merge-field parameters appended as URL query parameters. Values are resolved at runtime from the triggering CRM record using the merge-field format (for example, ${!Leads.Email}). Use the [Get Fields Metadata](fields.yaml#$.paths./settings/fields.get) resource to retrieve valid field API names.

user_defined_parameters.description: A single user-defined parameter appended as a URL query parameter. Note: The API uses plural 'user_defined_parameters' here but singular 'user_defined_parameter' in form_data_content - both are single objects, not arrays.

WebhooksAssociatedModuleReference.description: Represents a CRM module reference that has at least one webhook associated.

api_name.description: Represents the API name of the CRM module.

id.description: Represents the unique module identifier. Refer to the [Get Modules](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) resource for valid values.

WhatsappMessageNotificationTypeFollowupA.description: Represents the follow-up step configuration for a WhatsApp message notification action in a Cadence.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the WhatsApp message notification action.

type.description: Represents the action type for this follow-up step. Example: "whatsapp_message_notification".

WinnerConfigurationNested.description: Represents the winner declaration configuration for an AB test, including automatic announcement settings and the conversion percentage difference threshold.

announce_automatically.description: Indicates whether the winning form is announced automatically when the conversion percentage difference threshold is met. Possible values: **true** - The winner is announced automatically. **false** - The winner must be announced manually.

conversion_percentage_difference.description: Represents the minimum conversion rate percentage difference required to automatically declare a winner. Required when **announce_automatically** is **true**.

WorkflowActionCountsResponseSchema.description: Represents the response body containing the action count breakdown for one or more workflow rules, grouped by condition.

workflow_rules.description: Represents the array of workflow rule objects with their action count details.

WorkflowActionRef.description: Represents an action to execute within the approval process, identified by ID, name, and type.

name.description: Name of the action.

id.description: Id of the action. (Required)

type.description: action type which needs to be executed. (Required) Example: "field_updates".

WorkflowConditionActionCountSummarySchem.description: Represents the action count summary for a single workflow rule condition, including the condition ID, sequence number, and counts for instant and scheduled actions.

sequence_number.description: Represents the execution order of this condition within the workflow rule, starting from one.

oneOf.description: Represents a null value indicating no instant actions are configured for this condition.

scheduled_actions.description: Represents the array of scheduled action groups configured for this condition.

id.description: Represents the unique ID of the WorkflowConditionActionCountSummary within the workflow rule.

WorkflowConditionUsageSummarySchema.description: Represents the execution usage summary for a single workflow rule condition, including total execution count and breakdowns for instant and scheduled action groups.

scheduled_actions.description: Represents the array of scheduled action groups configured for this condition.

usage_count.description: Represents the total number of times the actions in this condition were executed.

id.description: Represents the unique ID of the WorkflowConditionUsageSummary within the workflow rule.

WorkflowConditionUsageWithTaggedInstantA.description: Represents the usage summary for a workflow rule condition where instant actions include tag-based metrics, along with scheduled action group data.

usage_count.description: Represents the total number of times the actions in this condition were executed.

id.description: Represents the unique ID of the WorkflowConditionUsageWithTaggedInstantActions within the workflow rule.

WorkflowConfigurationsAction.description: Represents an action type available for the module. Defines an operation that can be performed when a workflow rule triggers. The limit field is the per-type cap that applies independently to instant_actions and scheduled_actions - for instance, if limit=5, you can add up to 5 instances in instant_actions and up to 5 in scheduled_actions of the same rule.

is_clickable.description: Indicates whether this action type can be edited directly from the workflow configuration UI page. Not relevant for API usage.

associate_action.description: Indicates whether this action type is an associate action. Associate actions link or associate records between modules (for example, linking a Contact to a Deal or associating a Product with an Order). Associate actions differ from standard data-write actions such as field_updates or email_notifications. Possible values: **true** - This action type is an associate action. **false** - This action type is a standard non-associate action.

limit_per_action.description: Represents the maximum number of items within a single action instance. For example, add_tags and remove_tags allow a maximum of 10 tags per action. Returns null if no per-action item limit applies.

api_name.description: Represents the API identifier of the action type used when creating or modifying workflow rules (for example, field_updates, email_notifications, webhooks, assign_owner, add_tags, remove_tags, create_record, add_meeting, schedule_call, convert, functions, flow).

supported_in_scheduled_action.description: Indicates whether this action type can be used as a scheduled (time-delayed) action in a workflow rule. **Possible values:** true - This action type is supported in scheduled_actions (for example, time-delayed email_notifications or field_updates). false - This action type is only supported in instant_actions.

name.description: Represents the display name of the action type as shown in the CRM UI.

limit.description: Maximum number of instances of this action type allowed per workflow rule. Applies independently to instant_actions and scheduled_actions - for instance, if limit=5, you can add up to 5 instances in instant_actions and up to 5 in scheduled_actions. Returns LIMIT_EXCEEDED if exceeded.

WorkflowConfigurationsMetadata.description: Configuration metadata for workflows on a specific module. Contains three sections: triggers (events that fire the rule), actions (operations available when the rule fires with their per-type limits and scheduling support), and related_triggers_details (child/related modules like Notes or Calls whose events can also trigger rules on the parent module).

related_triggers_details.description: List of related modules (e.g., Notes, Calls, Activities) whose record events can trigger workflow rules on the parent module. Each entry contains the related module's identity and available trigger types.

triggers.description: Represents the list of trigger types available for the module. Each entry defines an event that can initiate a workflow rule, along with the action types supported for that trigger (for example, create, edit, delete, field_update, date_or_datetime).

actions.description: List of available action types for the module. Each action defines an operation that can be performed when the workflow rule fires, along with its per-type limit (applies independently to instant_actions and scheduled_actions), scheduling support, and whether it is an associate action (reusable entity referenced by ID) or non-associate action (defined inline).

WorkflowConfigurationsModuleReference.description: Represents a CRM module with its identity and display labels, including its API name, singular and plural display labels, unique ID, and internal name.

singular_label.description: Represents the singular display name of the module as shown in the CRM UI (for example, Lead, Contact, Deal).

plural_label.description: Represents the plural display name of the module as shown in the CRM UI (for example, Leads, Contacts, Deals).

api_name.description: Represents the API name of the CRM module used in API requests (for example, Leads, Contacts, Deals, Accounts, Tasks, Cases, Products, Quotes, Sales_Orders, Invoices, Campaigns, Vendors).

name.description: Represents the internal name of the CRM module.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the CRM module.

WorkflowConfigurationsRelatedTriggerDeta.description: Represents a related module that can act as a trigger source for the parent module's workflow rules. For example, when a user creates a Note on a Lead record, a workflow rule on the Leads module configured with a Notes-related trigger fires.

api_name.description: Represents the API name of the related module that can act as a trigger source (for example, Notes, Tasks, Events, Attachments). Use this value to identify the related module when creating workflow rules that should fire on related record events.

module.description: Module identity including api_name, id, and labels.

name.description: Represents the display name of the related module.

triggers.description: Represents the list of trigger types available from this related module. These triggers can be used in workflow rules on the parent module via the execute_when.details.trigger_module field.

WorkflowConfigurationsTrigger.description: A trigger type available for the module. Defines the event that initiates a workflow rule. Use the api_name value in the execute_when.type field when creating or updating a workflow rule via POST/PUT /settings/automation/workflow_rules.

api_name.description: Represents the API identifier of the trigger type. Use this value in the execute_when.type field when creating a workflow rule (for example, create, edit, create_or_edit, delete, field_update, section_update, date_or_datetime, score_increase, score_decrease, score_update).

deprecated.description: Indicates whether this trigger type is deprecated. Possible values: true - The trigger type is deprecated and should not be used for new workflow rules, though it may still appear on existing rules. false - The trigger type is active and available for use.

name.description: Represents the display name of the trigger type as shown in the CRM UI (for example, Create, Edit, FieldUpdate, DateBased).

scheduled_actions_supported.description: Indicates whether this trigger type supports scheduled (time-delayed) actions. Possible values: true - Both instant_actions and scheduled_actions are available for workflow rules with this trigger. false - Only instant_actions can be used in workflow rules with this trigger.

actions.description: Represents the list of action type API names supported by this trigger. Only these action types can be used in workflow rules with this trigger type. Cross-reference with the top-level actions array in the response for full action metadata, including per-type limits and scheduling support.

items.description: Represents an action type API name supported by this trigger (for example, field_updates, email_notifications, webhooks, assign_owner, add_tags, remove_tags, create_record, add_meeting, schedule_call, convert, functions, flow).

component_id.description: Represents the component identifier for marketplace or custom triggers. Returns null for standard built-in trigger types.

generated_type.description: Represents the generated type identifier for marketplace or custom triggers. Returns null for standard built-in trigger types.

WorkflowGroupedFilterCriterion.description: Represents a grouped filter criterion containing multiple simple filter conditions evaluated together using a logical operator such as AND or OR.

group.description: Represents the array of filter conditions to be evaluated together using the specified logical operator.

group_operator.description: Represents the logical operator applied between the filter conditions in the group.

WorkflowRuleActionCountGroupSchema.description: Represents the action count breakdown for a single workflow rule, encapsulating the rule ID and its associated condition-level action count groups.

id.description: Represents the unique ID of the WorkflowRuleActionCountGroup within the workflow rule.

conditions.description: Represents array of condition objects containing criteria and actions for this rule.

WorkflowRulePostNestedSchema.description: Represents the configuration object for a new workflow rule, including required fields such as name, target module, and trigger configuration.

name.description: Specify the workflow rule name. Required. Cannot exceed 100 characters. Special characters are not allowed.

description.description: Specify an optional description for the workflow rule. Set to null to clear an existing description.

module.description: The module to which the workflow rule applies. Use the [Get Modules API](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) to retrieve module IDs. Required. Must be a workflow-supported module. If both id and api_name are provided, they must match. Use `getWorkflowConfigurations` to discover supported modules. Cannot be changed after creation.

execute_when.description: Specifies when the workflow rule is triggered. This is a required JSON object with "type" and "details" properties. For example: {"type": "create_or_edit", "details": {"trigger_module": {"api_name": "Leads", "id": "..."}, "repeat": false}}. Passing a string instead of a JSON object, such as "create_or_edit", returns an "INVALID_DATA" error. The "details.trigger_module" must match the module associated with the workflow rule. Use "getWorkflowConfigurations" to retrieve the available triggers and their supported actions.

conditions.description: Specify the conditions that define the branching logic of the workflow rule. Each condition evaluates records against criteria and executes its own set of actions. At least one condition is required.

lock.description: Specify the lock configuration to prevent other users from editing the rule. Only administrators can lock or unlock rules.

message.description: Specify the reason or context for locking the rule. Valid only when **lock.status** is set to true.

status.description: Specify whether to lock the rule. Possible values: true - Locks the rule to prevent editing. false - Unlocks the rule.

WorkflowRuleProcessingSummary.description: Represents the summary of workflow rule impact for the job, including counts of total evaluated, processed, and failed rules.

WorkflowRulePutNestedSchema.description: Represents the configuration object for updating an existing workflow rule, including the rule ID and optional fields such as name, trigger, conditions, and lock status.

id.description: Represents the unique ID of the workflow rule to update. Required.

active.description: Specify whether the workflow rule is active or inactive. Possible values: true - The rule is active and executes when triggered. false - The rule is inactive and does not execute.

delete_schedule_action.description: Specify whether to delete all scheduled actions associated with the workflow rule when deactivating it. Possible values: true - Delete all scheduled actions when the rule is deactivated. false - Preserve scheduled actions when the rule is deactivated.

status.description: Specify the activation state of the workflow rule. When setting **active** to false, you can optionally delete all associated scheduled actions.

execute_when.description: Defines the conditions under which the workflow rule will be executed. (Required)

name.description: Specify the workflow rule name. Required.

description.description: Specify the workflow rule description.

conditions.description: Specify the array of condition objects to update. On update, unspecified conditions are preserved. Conditions with a null ID are added; conditions with an existing ID get replaced; conditions with a **_delete** flag are removed.

lock.description: Specify whether the workflow rule should be locked to prevent editing by other users.

message.description: Specify a note or label indicating the reason or context for locking the rule.

status.description: Specify whether to lock or unlock the workflow rule. Possible values: true - Locks the rule to prevent editing. false - Unlocks the rule.

WorkflowRuleReference.description: Represents a reference to the workflow rule that triggered a webhook execution.

name.description: Represents the display name of the workflow rule.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the workflow rule.

WorkflowRuleSingleGetResponseSchema.description: Represents the response body for a single workflow rule retrieval, containing a single-element array with the full rule details.

workflow_rules.description: Represents the array containing the single workflow rule retrieved.

WorkflowRuleSingleGetSchema.description: Represents the full configuration and metadata of a single workflow rule, including its trigger, conditions, actions, lock status, and audit timestamps.

created_time.description: Represents the ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when the system created this workflow rule.

editable.description: Indicates whether the requesting user has permission to edit this workflow rule.

deprecated.description: Indicates whether this workflow rule is deprecated and should be migrated to a newer configuration.

deletable.description: Indicates whether the requesting user has permission to delete this workflow rule.

description.description: Represents the user-defined description of the workflow rule. Null if not set.

source.description: Represents the origin of the workflow rule. For example, **crm** for rules created through the CRM UI, or **API** for rules created through the API.

last_executed_time.description: Represents the ISO 8601 timestamp of the last time this workflow rule was triggered. Null if the rule has never been triggered.

name.description: Represents the name of the workflow rule.

id.description: Represents the unique ID of the workflow rule.

category.description: Represents the classification category of the workflow rule.

conditions.description: Represents the array of condition objects that define the criteria for executing the actions of the workflow rule.

WorkflowRuleUsageResponseSchema.description: Represents the response body containing detailed execution usage metrics for one or more workflow rules within a queried date range.

workflow_rules.description: Represents the array of workflow rule usage objects.

items.description: Represents the usage report for a single workflow rule, including execution metrics at the condition level.

trigger_count.description: Represents the number of times this workflow rule was triggered within the queried date range.

name.description: Represents the name of the workflow rule.

id.description: Represents the unique ID of the workflow rule.

conditions.description: Represents the array of condition objects with usage metrics for the workflow rule.

reset_time.description: Represents the ISO 8601 timestamp when the usage counters were last reset.

WorkflowRulesAutomationAddMeetingDetails.description: add_meeting details; creates an Event when triggered. Events layouts/mandatory fields: GET /settings/layouts?module=Events; field IDs: GET /settings/fields?module=Events. Required: module (api_name='Events' or id), layout (id), field_mappings (1-25; include Event_Title and Start_DateTime), meeting_duration (unit: integer; period: hours|minutes; omit when All_Day=true), host_unavailable (assign_record_owner_as_host=true or assign_task with id). Optional: apply_restriction (boolean).

module.description: Target module for the meeting. Must be the Events module. Provide either api_name ("Events") or the Events module id.

layout.description: Layout to use when creating the Event record. Determines which fields are available and their validation rules. Fetch valid layouts from GET /settings/layouts?module=Events. The layout.id is required.

field_mappings.description: Maps values to Event fields. Include all layout-mandatory fields; common fields include Event_Title, Start_DateTime, All_Day, Participants, and Remind_At. End_DateTime is computed from Start_DateTime and meeting_duration; omit it. Types: static for literal text/picklists (not DateTime/ALARM); merge_field for text tokens (not lookups/owners); execution_time for Start_DateTime and Remind_At, with a sign for datetimes and periods days, business_days, hours, or minutes. If All_Day=true, use period days and omit meeting_duration.

items.description: Represents a single field-to-value mapping entry for the new Event record, conforming to the AutomationFieldMappings schema. Each entry identifies a target Event field and specifies the value resolution strategy: static for literal values, merge_field for runtime token substitution, or execution_time for dynamically resolved DateTime and ALARM fields.

meeting_duration.description: Duration of the meeting. Specifies a numeric value and time period (e.g., 1 hour, 30 minutes). Required when All_Day is not set to true in field_mappings. If All_Day is true, meeting_duration must not be provided - the API returns INVALID_DATA with field1/field2 conflict details.

host_unavailable.description: Fallback behavior when the designated meeting host is unavailable. Either assign the record owner as host (assign_record_owner_as_host=true) or create a follow-up task (assign_task with a pre-configured task ID). Exactly one option must be specified; providing both returns INVALID_DATA with field1/field2 conflict, providing neither returns EXPECTED_FIELD_MISSING.

apply_restriction.description: Whether to enforce assignment-threshold rules (record count limits per user) on the record owner when creating the Event record. When true, the system checks whether the owner has reached their record limit before creating the record. Only effective when the org has assignment thresholds configured.

id.description: Server-generated unique identifier for this add meeting action. Present only in GET responses; not required in POST requests.

WorkflowRulesAutomationCreateRecordDetai.description: PURPOSE: Details object for create_record action. Creates a record in a module with field values from static data, merge fields, or execution-time refs. NOT for Tasks/Events/Calls (use tasks, add_meeting, schedule_call). PREREQUISITES: GET /settings/modules for id. GET /settings/layouts?module={api_name} for layout + mandatory fields. GET /settings/fields?module={api_name} for field ids. MANDATORY: module ({api_name, id}), layout ({id}), field_mappings (array 1-25, include all mandatory fields). OPTIONAL: apply_restriction (bool). EXAMPLE: {"module": {"api_name": "Contacts", "id": "111111000000000129"}, "layout": {"id": "111111000000000403"}, "field_mappings": [{"field": {"api_name": "Last_Name"}, "type": "merge_field", "value": "${!Leads.Last_Name}"}]}

module.description: Target module in which the new record will be created. Supported modules: Leads, Contacts, Potentials (Deals), Accounts, Products, Cases, custom modules, and team modules. NOT supported: Tasks, Events, Calls - use add_meeting for Events and schedule_call for Calls. Fetch available modules from GET /settings/modules. At least api_name or id must be provided; always use the full 19-digit module ID as returned by the modules API.

layout.description: Layout to use when creating the record. Determines which fields are available and their validation rules. Fetch valid layouts from GET /settings/layouts?module={module_api_name}. The layout.id is required.

field_mappings.description: Field mappings for the new record. Each entry uses {"field":{"api_name":"Last_Name"},"type":"static","value":"Test"}. Include all mandatory fields (system_mandatory=true or api_mandatory=true from GET /settings/layouts?module={module}); otherwise, REQUIRED_DATA_NOT_FOUND. Types: static (not Date/DateTime/ALARM or unique fields), merge_field (not lookup/owner fields), execution_time (required for Date/DateTime/ALARM; supports days, business_days, hours, minutes; datetime requires a sign).

items.description: Represents a single field-to-value mapping entry for the new record, conforming to the AutomationFieldMappings schema. Each entry identifies the target field via a field reference and specifies the value resolution strategy through a type discriminator: static for literal values, merge_field for runtime token substitution, execution_time for dynamically resolved values, or composite for compound values.

apply_restriction.description: Whether to enforce assignment-threshold rules (record count limits per user) on the record owner when creating the record. When true, the system checks whether the owner has reached their record limit before creating the record. Only effective when the org has assignment thresholds configured.

id.description: Server-generated unique identifier for this create record action. Present only in GET responses; not required in POST requests.

WorkflowRulesAutomationFieldAttributes.description: Identifies the target CRM field to which a mapping value is applied within an automation rule. The api_name and ID properties must both be supplied and must refer to the same field; a mismatch between the two causes an AMBIGUITY_DURING_PROCESSING error. Available fields for a given module can be discovered via GET /settings/fields?module={api_name}.

api_name.description: Represents the API name of the target field in the destination module — for example, Subject, Due_Date, or Owner — used to identify the field receiving the mapped value within automation actions such as workflow tasks, create_record, and convert.

id.description: Represents the numeric identifier of the target CRM field. Used in conjunction with the field's API name, both of which must resolve to the same field for a mapping to be valid.

WorkflowRulesAutomationFieldMappings.description: Represents a single field-to-value mapping used within automation actions such as workflow tasks, create_record, add_meeting, and schedule_call. Each mapping identifies a target field via api_name or ID, declares a type discriminator that determines value interpretation, and supplies a value whose shape varies by type: static supplies a literal value, merge_field supplies a runtime-resolved token string, execution_time supplies a date or datetime offset object, and composite supplies structured participant data for the Events Participants field. The field_mappings array must include all fields the target module requires; omitting any produces a REQUIRED_DATA_NOT_FOUND error.

WorkflowRulesAutomationLayoutRef.description: PURPOSE: Layout reference for create_record, add_meeting, schedule_call actions. MANDATORY: id (string). Determines field availability and validation rules. GET /settings/layouts?module={api_name} to discover.

id.description: Unique layout ID. Required. Obtain from GET /settings/layouts?module={module_api_name}.

name.description: Display name of the layout. Optional in requests; present in GET responses.

display_label.description: Human-readable label of the layout. Present in GET responses.

WorkflowRulesAutomationModuleRef.description: PURPOSE: Module reference used across non-associate actions. At least one of api_name or id required (EXPECTED_FIELD_MISSING if neither). If both given, must match (AMBIGUITY_DURING_PROCESSING). GET /settings/modules to discover. Always use full 19-digit module ID.

api_name.description: API name of the module (e.g., Leads, Contacts, Deals, Vendors).

id.description: Unique module ID (19-digit format). Always use the full ID as returned by GET /settings/modules - truncated or shortened IDs return INVALID_DATA ('the tabId given seems to be invalid'). Optional in requests if api_name is provided; always present in responses.

WorkflowRulesAutomationScheduleCallDetai.description: PURPOSE: Details object for schedule_call action. Creates a Call record when workflow fires. PREREQUISITES: GET /settings/layouts?module=Calls for layout + mandatory fields. GET /settings/fields?module=Calls for field ids. MANDATORY: module ({api_name: 'Calls', id}), layout ({id}), field_mappings (array 1-25, include Subject, Call_Type). OPTIONAL: apply_restriction (bool). KEY FIELDS: Subject, Call_Type ('Outbound'|'Inbound'|'Missed'), Call_Purpose, Call_Start_Time, Remind_At.

module.description: Target module for the call. Must be the Calls module. Provide either api_name ("Calls") or the Calls module id.

layout.description: Layout to use when creating the Call record. Determines which fields are available and their validation rules. Fetch valid layouts from GET /settings/layouts?module=Calls. The layout.id is required.

field_mappings.description: Maps values to Call fields. Include all layout-mandatory fields; Call_Type is system-mandatory (Outbound, Inbound, or Missed), and omitting it returns REQUIRED_DATA_NOT_FOUND. Common fields: Subject, Call_Type, Call_Purpose, Call_Start_Time, Remind_At. Types: static for literal text/picklists (not DateTime/ALARM); merge_field for text tokens (not lookups/owners); execution_time for Call_Start_Time and Remind_At, with a sign for datetimes and periods days, business_days, hours, or minutes.

items.description: Represents a single field-to-value mapping entry for the new Call record, conforming to the AutomationFieldMappings schema. Each entry identifies a target Call field and specifies the value resolution strategy: static for literal values, merge_field for runtime token substitution, or execution_time for dynamically resolved DateTime and ALARM fields.

apply_restriction.description: Whether to enforce assignment-threshold rules (record count limits per user) on the record owner when creating the Call record. When true, the system checks whether the owner has reached their record limit before creating the record. Only effective when the org has assignment thresholds configured.

id.description: Server-generated unique identifier for this schedule call action. Present only in GET responses; not required in POST requests.

WorkflowRulesCompositeFieldMapping.description: Represents a composite-type field mapping used exclusively for the Participants field in the Events module via the add_meeting action. The value carries a structured object that encodes participant data and is not applicable to any other field or automation action type.

display_value.description: The server-computed representation of the mapped value, included in GET responses. Omitted from create and update requests.

field.description: Target field to populate when the automation executes. api_name is required. If id is also provided, both must refer to the same field; otherwise the API returns AMBIGUITY_DURING_PROCESSING.

type.description: Serves as the polymorphic discriminator that identifies this field mapping as a composite mapping; the value must be set to "composite" to select this schema variant.

value.description: Holds the structured composite object that encodes participant data for the Events module Participants field; the shape of this object varies according to the participant type configuration defined for the automation rule.

WorkflowRulesCountResponseSchema.description: Represents the response body containing the organization-level workflow rule quota and current usage counts.

rules_count.description: Represents the workflow rule count and limit details for the organization.

scheduled_actions_per_rule_limit.description: Represents the maximum number of scheduled action groups allowed per workflow rule.

total_rules_limit.description: Represents the maximum total number of workflow rules allowed in the organization.

active_rules_configured.description: Represents the number of currently active workflow rules configured in the organization.

rules_per_process_limit.description: Represents the maximum number of workflow rules allowed per business process.

total_actions_per_rule_limit.description: Represents the maximum total number of actions (instant and scheduled combined) allowed per workflow rule.

total_rules_limit_per_module.description: Represents the maximum number of workflow rules allowed per CRM module.

active_rules_limit.description: Represents the maximum number of active workflow rules allowed in the organization.

total_rules_configured.description: Represents the total number of workflow rules configured in the organization, including both active and inactive rules.

active_rules_limit_per_module.description: Represents the maximum number of active workflow rules allowed per CRM module.

WorkflowRulesExecutionTimeFieldMapping.description: Represents an execution_time-type field mapping that computes a date, datetime, or ALARM value at runtime by applying a signed offset to a trigger field or the current time. The value carries an ExecutionTimeValue object specifying the period, unit, trigger_field, and optional time or notify_type properties. A plus sign places the result after the trigger; a minus sign places it before. ALARM fields always require minus. Workflow task actions support only days and business_days as period values.

display_value.description: The server-computed representation of the mapped value, included in GET responses. Omitted from create and update requests.

field.description: Target field to populate when the automation executes. api_name is required. If id is also provided, both must refer to the same field; otherwise the API returns AMBIGUITY_DURING_PROCESSING.

type.description: Identifies the mapping variant as an execution-time offset. The value is always "execution_time" for this schema and acts as the polymorphic discriminator across the AutomationFieldMappings union.

value.description: Execution-time object specifying how to compute the date/datetime offset from a reference field.

WorkflowRulesExecutionTimeValue.description: Represents the offset configuration used by an execution_time mapping to compute a final date, datetime, or ALARM value at runtime. Contains period (the time unit granularity), unit (the numeric magnitude expressed as a string integer), and trigger_field (a merge token or ${CURRENTTIME}). Date fields use period, unit, and trigger_field with an implied positive direction. Datetime fields additionally accept sign to control direction. ALARM fields additionally accept time and notify_type, and always require a minus sign. Workflow task actions restrict period to days or business_days.

period.description: The calendar or time unit applied to the offset. Possible values: **days** — counts all calendar days including weekends and holidays; supported by every action type. **business_days** — excludes weekends and requires the organisation's business-day setting to be enabled; supported by all action types. **hours** — available only for create_record, add_meeting, and schedule_call. **minutes** — available only for create_record, add_meeting, and schedule_call. workflow_tasks accept only **days** or **business_days**.

unit.description: The number of period units to offset from the trigger date, supplied as a non-negative integer string (for example, "1", "30"). Passing "0" produces a same-day result, such as scheduling a Remind_At on the same day as the due date.

sign.description: The direction of the offset relative to the trigger date. Possible values: **plus** — places the computed value after the trigger (for example, a due date two days after record creation). **minus** — places the computed value before the trigger (for example, a reminder one day before the due date). For datetime fields (data_type=datetime) a value is expected; omitting it returns a DEPENDENT_FIELD_MISSING error. For date-only fields (data_type=date) the value defaults to **plus** when absent. When targeting Remind_At (data_type=ALARM), **minus** is the only applicable direction.

trigger_field.description: The reference date or datetime field from which the offset is measured. Accepts a merge-field token that resolves to a Date or DateTime field on the parent module (for example, "${!Leads.Modified_Time}", "${!Tasks.Due_Date}"), or the reserved constant "${CURRENTTIME}" to use the automation execution timestamp. When computing a Remind_At (ALARM) value, "${!Tasks.Due_Date}" is the typical anchor.

time.description: The time-of-day component of the computed value, expressed in 24-hour HH:mm format (for example, "13:00", "01:30"). Applies when the target field carries data type datetime or ALARM (as reported by GET /settings/fields). Supplying this property for a date-only field (data_type=date) produces a validation error.

notify_type.description: The notification channel used to deliver the reminder. Applies exclusively when the target field carries data type ALARM (i.e., Remind_At); date and datetime fields do not use this property. Possible values: **popup** — triggers an in-app notification. **email** — sends a message to the task owner. **emailandpopup** — delivers both simultaneously.

WorkflowRulesFilterFieldBase.description: Represents the base field reference used in filter operations, containing minimal required properties. The field's data_type is not part of this object; resolve it from the corresponding FieldSchema. For formula fields, use formula.return_type as the effective data_type; for rollup_summary fields, use rollup_summary.return_type.

id.description: Represents the unique ID of the field used for filter operations.

api_name.description: Represents the API name of the field used for filter application. Supports relationship notation, for example, Deals__r.Stage.

WorkflowRulesGetResponseSchema.description: Represents the paginated list response for workflow rules, containing an array of workflow rule objects and pagination metadata.

workflow_rules.description: Represents the array of workflow rule objects returned in the list response.

WorkflowRulesMergeFieldMapping.description: Represents a merge_field-type mapping whose value is resolved at execution time by substituting token references with live field data. Supports direct field tokens (${!Module.Field}), traversal tokens (${!Module.Lookup.Field}), and system tokens (${CURRENTTIME}, ${CURRENTUSER}). Applies to text-based fields such as Subject, Description, and custom text fields. Targeting owner or lookup fields with this type produces a DEPENDENT_MISMATCH error; those fields require a static mapping using an object with a numeric identifier and an optional name. Multiple tokens may be chained with surrounding text for multi-line fields, while single-value fields such as email or URL accept exactly one token.

display_value.description: The server-computed representation of the mapped value, included in GET responses. Omitted from create and update requests.

field.description: Target field to populate when the automation executes. api_name is required. If id is also provided, both must refer to the same field; otherwise the API returns AMBIGUITY_DURING_PROCESSING.

type.description: Identifies the mapping strategy for this field assignment. The value must be `merge_field`, which instructs the automation engine to resolve the field value dynamically from a merge field token at execution time rather than from a static literal.

value.description: A string containing one or more ${!...} merge-field tokens resolved at runtime.

allow_agent_user.description: Controls whether agent users are eligible for record assignment. Possible values: **true** — agent users are included in the assignment pool alongside standard users. **false** — agent users are excluded from assignment. Applies to mapping types role, group, profile, merge_field, and criteria. Does not apply to user or assignment_rule types.

WorkflowRulesMergeFieldStringValue.description: Represents the string value carried by a merge_field mapping, containing one or more runtime-resolved token references. Supports direct field tokens (${!Module.Field}), lookup traversal tokens (${!Module.Lookup.Field}), and system tokens (${CURRENTTIME}, ${CURRENTUSER}). Tokens may be combined with surrounding text for multi-line field targets. Fields that hold a single typed value such as email or URL accept exactly one token.

WorkflowRulesSimpleFilterCriterionValueO.description: Represents the base minified record structure of a lookup module, containing the record's unique identifier and display name.

id.description: Represents the unique ID of the lookup module record.

name.description: Represents the display name of the lookup module record.

WorkflowRulesStaticArrayValue.description: Represents an array of string values used as the static value for multiselectpicklist fields, where each element corresponds to an available picklist option. Valid option labels are retrievable from the GET /settings/fields endpoint filtered by data_type=multiselectpicklist.

items.description: A single picklist option string to include in the multi-select field value. Each entry corresponds to one selectable option as defined for the target field in Zoho CRM.

WorkflowRulesStaticFieldMapping.description: Represents a static-type mapping that assigns a literal value directly to the target field at execution time. The value shape varies by field data type: a plain string for text, picklist, phone, email, URL, number, decimal, currency, and percentage fields (numeric values expressed as strings); an array of strings for multiselectpicklist fields; and an object containing ID and name for ownerlookup fields. Date, datetime, and ALARM fields do not support this type — use execution_time instead, as static on those fields produces a DEPENDENT_MISMATCH error. Fields marked unique in the module settings also require merge_field rather than static for create_record actions.

display_value.description: The server-computed representation of the mapped value, included in GET responses. Omitted from create and update requests.

field.description: Target field to populate when the automation executes. api_name is required. If id is also provided, both must refer to the same field; otherwise the API returns AMBIGUITY_DURING_PROCESSING.

type.description: Identifies the mapping strategy for this field assignment. The value must be `static`, which instructs the automation engine to assign a fixed, literal value to the target field at execution time rather than resolving it dynamically.

value.description: The literal value assigned to the target field at automation execution time. The expected shape is determined by the target field data_type, discoverable via GET /settings/fields?module={module}. For most field types, supply a string (for example, "High", "Not Started", "1234"). For multi-select picklist fields (data_type: multiselectpicklist), supply an array of option strings. For fields that reference an entity such as an owner or layout (data_type: ownerlookup), supply an object with at minimum the entity ID.

WorkflowRulesStaticObjectValue.description: Represents an object value used as the static value for ownerlookup and layout fields, containing an ID that identifies the target user or layout and an optional name that the server resolves from the ID when not supplied. Typically used to assign record ownership by providing the user ID.

id.description: The system identifier of the referenced entity, such as a user or layout record. This value drives entity resolution by the automation engine and must be provided when the target field references an entity.

name.description: The display name of the referenced entity, such as a user full name or a layout label. When omitted from a request payload, the server resolves and populates this property from the supplied ID. The property is present in all GET responses.

WorkflowRulesStaticStringValue.description: Represents a plain string value used as the static value for text, picklist, phone, email, URL, number, decimal, currency, and percentage fields. Numeric values are expressed as strings rather than numeric literals. Picklist values must exactly match one of the options defined for the field.

WorkflowSimpleFilterCriterion.description: Represents a simple filter criterion for workflow rule queries, specifying the field API name, comparator, and value to match.

allOf.description: Represents additional field reference constraints for the filter criterion, requiring the `api_name` property to identify the target field.

field.description: Represents the field to which the filter criterion is applied.

comparator.description: Represents the comparison operator applied to the filter criterion. **${ANYVALUE}** is a special value supported only in field update triggers; it matches any change to the monitored field value.

type.description: Indicates whether the criterion value is a direct value or a system variable placeholder.

WorkflowSuccessSchema.description: Represents the success response returned after creating a workflow rule, containing the result details of the created rule.

workflow_rules.description: Represents the array of workflow rule objects returned in the success response.

WorkflowTasksModuleDetails.description: Contains module metadata, including labels, API name, IDs, and optional module_name for related module contexts.

singular_label.description: Singular display label of the module (e.g., Lead, Contact).

moduleName.description: Module display name (camelCase). Present on parent module objects only.

id.description: Unique Zoho CRM module ID.

plural_label.description: Plural display label of the module (e.g., Leads, Contacts).

api_name.description: API name of the module used in API requests (e.g., Leads, Contacts, Deals).

per_page.description: Maximum number of records/actions requested per page.

count.description: Number of records/actions returned in the current response page.

page.description: Current page number in the paginated result set (typically reflects the requested page value).

more_records.description: Indicates whether additional records/actions are available beyond the current page.

value.description: The literal value assigned to the target field at automation execution time. The expected shape is determined by the target field data_type, discoverable via GET /settings/fields?module={module}. For most field types, supply a string (for example, "High", "Not Started", "1234"). For multi-select picklist fields (data_type: multiselectpicklist), supply an array of option strings. For fields that reference an entity such as an owner or layout (data_type: ownerlookup), supply an object with at minimum the entity ID.

WorkflowTasksStaticObjectValue.description: Represents an object value used as the static value for ownerlookup and layout fields, containing an ID that identifies the target user or layout and an optional name that the server resolves from the ID when not supplied. Typically used to assign record ownership by providing the user ID.

id.description: The system identifier of the referenced entity, such as a user or layout record. This value drives entity resolution by the automation engine and must be provided when the target field references an entity.

name.description: The display name of the referenced entity, such as a user full name or a layout label. When omitted from a request payload, the server resolves and populates this property from the supplied ID. The property is present in all GET responses.

WorkflowTasksStaticStringValue.description: Represents a plain string value used as the static value for text, picklist, phone, email, URL, number, decimal, currency, and percentage fields. Numeric values are expressed as strings rather than numeric literals. Picklist values must exactly match one of the options defined for the field.

ZiaSuggestedUsersTypeAssignToObject.description: If assign to type is zia suggested user.

type.description: Defines the type or users to associate as owner during execution. Possible values: **zia_suggested_users** - Represents zia suggested users. Example: "zia_suggested_users".

ZiaSuggestedUsersTypeAssignToRequestObje.description: Assigns ownership using Zia AI suggestions. No resource configuration needed.

type.description: Assign to type IDentifier. Must be 'zia_suggested_users'. Possible values: **zia_suggested_users** - Represents zia suggested users. Example: "zia_suggested_users".

ZohoFlowActionSchema.description: Represents a non-associate action that triggers a Zoho Flow workflow when the workflow rule condition is met.

name.description: Represents the display name of the Zoho Flow action. This field is required.

type.description: Represents the action type discriminator that identifies this as a Zoho Flow action within the workflow rule.

details.description: Configuration for the Zoho Flow action. Requires the ID and name of the custom action to trigger in Zoho Flow.

id.description: Represents the unique ID of the Zoho Flow action within the workflow rule.

_delete.description: Indicates that this Zoho Flow action should be removed from the workflow rule when set in a PUT request. Provide a null value to signal deletion.
